faqs.question: What is the BWB XP used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 5-channel flame photometer used for simultaneous measurement of sodium, potassium, lithium, calcium, and caesium, applied across clinical, pharmaceutical, environmental, and industrial elemental analysis.

faqs.question: How is BWB XP different from other flame photometers?
faqs.answer: It's the first and only flame photometer offering simultaneous detection and display of all five elements from a single dilution, removing the filter-change-and-recalibrate cycle every other flame photometer design has required since 1951.

faqs.question: Does each element need a separate sample dilution?
faqs.answer: No. All five elements are measured from a single dilution.

faqs.question: What gas does the instrument require?
faqs.answer: Propane, LPG, or butane.

faqs.question: Does it need a separate air supply?
faqs.answer: No. A built-in air compressor is included, so connecting gas is the only requirement.

faqs.question: What's included with the instrument?
faqs.answer: Solutions and labware ship as standard, along with the built-in compressor — accessories BWB notes other manufacturers often sell separately.

faqs.question: How does data leave the instrument?
faqs.answer: Via USB to a connected PC, with support for intranet or internet-linked distributed reporting across multiple sites.

faqs.question: Does BWB XP correct for interference between elements?
faqs.answer: Yes. Calcium readings are automatically corrected for interference from high sodium levels.

faqs.question: Is IQ/OQ/PQ certification available?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a web-based standard offering, which BWB describes as unique in the analytical instrumentation market.

faqs.question: Can results be reported in different units?
faqs.answer: Yes. Five user-selectable units of measure are available, with selectable decimal places.

faqs.question: Is a printer available?
faqs.answer: Yes, as an integrated option using readily available standard paper.

faqs.question: How is the instrument constructed?
faqs.answer: Metal casework using RoHS-compliant components and materials wherever possible, designed to be portable and recyclable.

faqs.question: How long has BWB XP been in production?
faqs.answer: Since 2006, as BWB Technologies' flagship flame photometer model.

paragraphs: Every flame photometer design from 1951 onward has shared the same workflow: measure one element, change the filter, recalibrate, measure the next. Across five elements, that's five setups per sample. BWB XP was built from the ground up specifically to remove that repetition, detecting and displaying all five elements — sodium, potassium, lithium, calcium, and caesium — from one dilution and one flame simultaneously.

The practical effect compounds across a batch. A lab running fifty samples for a five-element panel isn't running two hundred and fifty sequential measurements; it's running fifty. Operator-independent result determination means the output doesn't drift with who's running the instrument that day, and the step-by-step interface keeps a less experienced analyst on the correct procedure without hand-holding.

body: What ships standard, and where the data goes.

BWB's stated position is that other manufacturers charge extra for accessories the instrument actually needs to function; BWB XP ships with solutions, labware, and a built-in air compressor as standard. The only thing the lab supplies is gas — propane, LPG, or butane.

Data leaves the instrument over USB to a connected PC, which BWB frames specifically around distributed control: multi-national companies, universities, and government agencies running the same instrument model across sites benefit from output that ties into a company intranet or the internet rather than staying local to the bench. IQ/OQ/PQ certification is available web-based, which BWB positions as unique in the analytical instrumentation space — relevant wherever qualification documentation is a purchasing requirement rather than a nice-to-have.

paragraphs: Any flame photometer's calibration can drift over a long session — small changes in flame conditions, aspiration rate, or sample delivery accumulate quietly and show up as error in later readings. XP Plus addresses that directly rather than relying on periodic manual recalibration: an Internal Reference Standard, set to either caesium or lithium, runs alongside the four primary channels and acts as an internal standard, adjusting for those small changes as they occur.

The choice between caesium and lithium as the reference matters in practice. If lithium is one of the elements actually being measured in the sample, caesium is the sensible reference so the two don't interfere. Where lithium isn't a target analyte, it becomes available as the reference instead. Either way, the correction happens inline, during calibration and measurement, rather than being caught only when a check standard is re-run.

sections.title: Choosing Between XP and XP Plus
sections.tabSummary: Five raw channels versus four with drift correction
body: Five raw channels against four with drift correction.

The two instruments share the same underlying platform, the same removal of the filter-change cycle, and the same standard inclusions. The difference is what they're built to prioritize. BWB XP measures five elements simultaneously — sodium, potassium, lithium, calcium, and caesium — with no internal reference; caesium is a full measurement channel, not a correction mechanism. XP Plus trades that fifth channel for the IRS: four elements measured simultaneously, with caesium or lithium held back specifically to monitor and correct calibration drift.

Which one fits depends on what the panel actually needs. A lab that routinely reports caesium as a result wants XP. A lab running long batch sessions where calibration stability matters more than a fifth data point, or one that values the internal check IRS provides, wants XP Plus.

paragraphs: Most flame photometers measure whatever solution is presented to them, with calibration standards the lab has to source and prepare separately. BWB BIO ships with 5-point calibration standards for urine and 6-point standards for serum included as standard — matched to the two sample types clinical and renal research labs actually run, rather than generic multi-element standards adapted after the fact.

The Automatic Fluid Handling System extends that same logic to sample handling itself. It was originally designed specifically to work with the BIO unit, and it's configured through the same FP-PC software that manages calibration curves and generates reports, rather than as a bolt-on accessory with its own separate control layer. Together with an IRS option — caesium or lithium — correcting drift during calibration and measurement, the instrument is built around the realities of running blood and urine samples at volume rather than adapted to them.

faqs.question: What models are available?
faqs.answer: FL-C (Ca), FL-K (K), FL-L (Li), FL-N (Na), FL-2 (Na & K), FL-3 (Na, K & Li), and FL-4 (Na, K, Li & Ca).

faqs.question: Can I buy a single-element version?
faqs.answer: Yes. FL-C, FL-K, FL-L, and FL-N each measure only one element, avoiding the cost of unused channels.

faqs.question: How is Flash different from BWB XP?
faqs.answer: XP is a fixed 5-channel instrument (Na, K, Li, Ca, Cs). Flash is configurable across seven models from one to four channels, sharing XP's core no-filter-change engineering at a lower entry cost, but without a caesium channel or IRS option.

faqs.question: Does Flash include an Internal Reference Standard?
faqs.answer: No. IRS (caesium or lithium reference) is available on XP Plus and BIO, not on Flash.

faqs.question: What display does it use?
faqs.answer: A 5-inch touchscreen, compatible with most disposable laboratory gloves.

faqs.question: Does it need a separate air supply?

faqs.question: What gas does it require?
faqs.answer: Propane, LPG, or butane.

faqs.question: Are calibration standards included?
faqs.answer: Yes, supplied as standard at 10,000ppm concentration.

faqs.question: How does auto-read technology work?
faqs.answer: It enables operator-independent determination of results, reducing variability between different users running the same measurement.

faqs.question: Is Flash more efficient than previous BWB models?
faqs.answer: Yes. BWB states 13% lower gas consumption and 26% lower electricity consumption (kWh) compared to previous model generations.

faqs.question: Is IQ/OQ/PQ certification available?
faqs.answer: Yes, web-based, and BWB positions this as unique in the analytical instrumentation arena.

faqs.question: What's included with the instrument?
faqs.answer: Complete basic labware, calibration standards at 10,000ppm, and the built-in compressor and regulator.

faqs.question: How does data leave the instrument?

sections.tabSummary: When lithium alone is the right answer
body: When lithium alone is the right answer.

Most flame photometry work needs a panel, sodium and potassium alongside lithium, or the full electrolyte set including calcium. BWB LI is the exception: it exists for the specific case where lithium accuracy is the entire requirement, and where any other element would be a distraction from the one measurement that actually matters.

That's a narrower use case than BIO AV (which measures Na, K, and Li together with enhanced lithium detection) or the standard BIO and XP Plus panels. Where the work genuinely never needs sodium or potassium as a reported result — a dedicated lithium QC line, a research programme built entirely around lithium pharmacokinetics — BWB LI's concentrated design has no panel-instrument equivalent in accuracy terms. Where sodium or potassium are needed even occasionally, one of BWB's multi-element instruments is the better fit.

faqs.question: What is the BWB SOIL used for?
faqs.answer: It's a flame photometer purpose-built for agriculture, measuring sodium, potassium, and calcium in soil substrates and fertilisers, usable in either a laboratory or field setting.

faqs.question: Why was BWB SOIL developed?
faqs.answer: It builds on 2017 research by Professor Akiharu Sasaki establishing the specific case for flame photometry in agricultural analysis, developed further in conjunction with field requests and operational requirements from agricultural users.

faqs.question: Which elements does it measure?
faqs.answer: Sodium, potassium, and calcium, simultaneously, with enhanced calcium detection optimised for soil and fertiliser matrices.

faqs.question: Can it be used outside a laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's designed for genuine field portability, including setup in the back of a van, and can conduct on-site analysis at various geographical locations.

faqs.question: What does "just add gas" mean for field use?
faqs.answer: The instrument requires minimal setup infrastructure at the sample site, needing only a gas connection to run.

faqs.question: Does it produce a record of field results?
faqs.answer: Yes. A thermal printer is fitted as standard, maintaining traceability for sample analysis throughout field work.

faqs.question: What is the Internal Reference Standard (IRS) option?
faqs.answer: Lithium can be used as an internal reference standard, correcting small changes during calibration and measurement.

faqs.question: How is sample handling configured?
faqs.answer: Either through the BWB collection cup feature for manual introduction, or the AFHS automated sample handling system for higher-volume operation.

faqs.question: How is BWB SOIL different from BWB XP or XP Plus?
faqs.answer: XP and XP Plus are general-purpose bench instruments optimised for lab throughput across broader element panels. SOIL trades some of that panel breadth (no caesium channel, lithium available only as IRS) for enhanced calcium detection and genuine field portability specific to agricultural work.

faqs.question: Does it correct for interference between elements?
faqs.answer: Yes. Calcium readings are automatically corrected for interference from high sodium levels.

faqs.question: Is IQ/OQ/PQ certification available?
faqs.answer: Yes, web-based.

faqs.question: Can results be reported in different units?
faqs.answer: Yes. Four user-selectable units of measure are available, with selectable decimal places.

faqs.question: What platform is BWB SOIL built on?
faqs.answer: The footprint of the award-winning BWB XP, optimised beyond the original design specifically for agricultural analysis.

paragraphs: Every other instrument in BWB's range is a bench device. BWB SOIL is built to leave the bench entirely: a "just add gas" configuration and physical portability that allows the instrument to be set up in the back of a van and run field analysis on-site at various geographical locations.

That matters directly for agricultural sampling programmes, where the alternative is bagging soil samples, transporting them back to a lab, and waiting for results before a fertilisation or amendment decision can be made. Running the analysis at the point of sampling collapses that gap. A thermal printer fitted as standard keeps traceability intact throughout — every sample analysed in the field produces a physical record, which matters for advisory work, research documentation, and any context where field results need to be defensible after the fact.

body: What the Sasaki research established and how SOIL follows from it.

Flame photometry has measured potassium in fertilisers and soil substrates for decades, but that use largely happened on instruments built for other purposes. Professor Akiharu Sasaki's 2017 research made the case specifically for flame photometer analysis in agriculture, over and above other methods of analysis — establishing not just that the method works, but that it has particular advantages in this application.

BWB SOIL is the instrument that followed. Built on the BWB XP footprint and developed in conjunction with field requests and operational requirements from agricultural users, it takes the base platform's proven reliability and optimises it beyond the original design brief specifically for fertiliser and soil substrate work. Enhanced calcium detection reflects that — a channel tuned for the calcium behaviour actually found in soil and fertiliser matrices, not a generic setting borrowed from a clinical or industrial configuration.

body: Field and lab work don't always call for the same sample handling approach. BWB SOIL supports both: the BWB collection cup feature for direct, manual sample introduction, suited to field conditions where simplicity and speed matter more than automation, or the Automatic Fluid Handling System (AFHS) for labs running higher sample volumes where automated handling reduces manual steps.

The choice isn't fixed at purchase in the way it might be on a dedicated bench instrument — it's a configuration decision matched to how and where the instrument is actually being used, which is consistent with SOIL's broader design premise of adapting to field and lab conditions on the same platform rather than forcing one workflow across both.

longForm.heroLead: For decades, a handful of traditional flame photometer manufacturers served the sugar refining industry, and their robust units are now coming out of service one by one. BWB SUGAR was requested and designed specifically for the global sugar production marketplace to fill that gap — not a general instrument adapted for sugar refining, but one built at the industry's own request. It follows globally accepted published research on flame photometry in sugar refining dating from 1977 forward, with a specialised potassium and sodium detection channel — described by BWB as both a "uniquely hybridized dual channel" and, in the same source material, "a single channel of precise and accurate potassium and sodium measurement." Whichever framing applies to the exact hardware, the outcome is extreme accuracy across the working range of potassium control that refining processes depend on. This isn't a batch-sample instrument. It runs online, 24/7, continuously fed through BWB's proprietary Collection Cup system at a customer-provided feed of roughly 5ml/minute, with a 4-20mA 2-wire output compatible with SCADA software for direct integration into plant process control. The FP/PC app extends that further: real-time distributed control from a centralized location anywhere in the world, monitoring multiple refinery sites without staff on-site.

paragraphs: Every other BWB instrument in the range measures a discrete sample, one dilution at a time. BWB SUGAR doesn't work that way — it's built to sit on a process line and measure continuously, with potassium and sodium detection available online 24/7 rather than as a periodic check.

That continuity depends on the Collection Cup system, which provides real-time sample access to the mixing chamber and detection system from a constant condensation stream feed. The requirement is straightforward on the plant side: sample at or near ambient temperature, supplied by the customer at approximately 5ml/minute. From there, a 4-20mA 2-wire output feeds directly into SCADA software, so the measurement becomes part of the plant's existing process control loop rather than a separate reading someone has to check manually and re-enter.

body: What the FP/PC app actually connects.

For a sugar company running refineries across multiple countries, having genuine expertise physically present at every site is rarely practical. BWB describes the FP/PC app as a totally unique feature specifically because of what it removes: the need for staff to be on-site at all.

Multiple installation details share via intranet or internet links, so a single control room, based anywhere in the world, can apply centralized expertise to instrumentation running across every connected refinery. Data accumulates and can be analysed in real time, with virtually limitless capacity. Beneath that, .csv export lets individual sites or the central team build their own proprietary Excel-based reporting and share results quickly, without depending on a single fixed report format.

faqs.question: What is the BWB Nuclear used for?
faqs.answer: It's a flame photometer built specifically for low-concentration lithium measurement in nuclear power stations, most commonly for reactor coolant chemistry monitoring.

faqs.question: Does it measure elements other than lithium?
faqs.answer: No. All four detection channels measure lithium; none are allocated to other elements.

faqs.question: Why does it have four channels for one element?
faqs.answer: Each channel is independently calibrated within its own range of interest, which increases accuracy across the working concentration span in keeping with nuclear industry demand.

faqs.question: How was BWB Nuclear developed?
faqs.answer: It was designed in conjunction with Mr. Wolfgang Glock, BWB's distributor in Germany, bringing field-specific expertise into the design.

faqs.question: Can it run continuously rather than as a batch instrument?
faqs.answer: Yes, optionally. The Collection Cup feature converts the instrument into a 24/7, real-time online analyser.

faqs.question: Can it integrate with plant SCADA systems?
faqs.answer: Yes. One of the four channels ties to a 2-wire 4-20mA output that integrates seamlessly with any SCADA system, set to client protocols.

faqs.question: How does data get shared with teams away from the instrument?
faqs.answer: Via BWB's FP-PC app, sharing data over the internet or intranet.

faqs.question: What calibration solution and consumables are included?
faqs.answer: 10,000ppm calibration solution, sufficient to make 15 litres of 100ppm working solution, plus 1ml and 10ml pipettes (10 of each), 100 x 20ml sample cups, and a 100ml flask.

faqs.question: Is IQ/OQ/PQ certification available?
faqs.answer: Yes, web-based, relevant to nuclear industry regulatory documentation.

faqs.question: How is BWB Nuclear different from BWB LI?
faqs.answer: Both dedicate detection entirely to lithium, but differently. BWB LI concentrates detection design into fewer, highly optimised channels for general high accuracy. BWB Nuclear uses four channels, each independently calibrated to a specific range, suited to applications like reactor coolant chemistry where the concentration band is narrow and known.

faqs.question: Is the Collection Cup feature exclusive to this instrument?
faqs.answer: No. BWB describes it as totally unique to their range and available across all models, not exclusive to Nuclear.
